text:
Jamal: quick heads-up — seeing steady memory growth in KV during long-ctx runs after yesterday's key-sanitizer rollout. repro on canary with seq_len ~9k.

Alex: can you paste the profiler output / quick stats?

Jamal: pasted sample below (trimmed):
```
time: 2026-02-14T11:03:12Z
kv_hits: 1_240
kv_misses: 5_880
unique_keys_30m: 68_200
avg_key_bytes: 72
reuse_rate_per_request: 0.18
reuse_rate_for_session_affine: 0.12
previous_canary_reuse_rate: 0.72
heap_growth: +220MB over 30m under steady traffic
```

Maria: :thinking_face: reuse_rate dropping that far is alarming. we only changed the sanitizer to canonicalize weird utf8 and add a per-request fingerprint in one path. was that fingerprint supposed to be per-session?

Jamal: looks like one code path (message->prefix builder) flips to `request_fingerprint` when fallback sanitizer fires. that makes keys unique across requests instead of stable session prefixes.

Sophie: could also explain fragmentation — new keys blow out the hotset and cause more evictions -> more paging. batching heuristics will miss coalescing when prefixes differ.

Alex: i ran `pprof` on the canary: most allocations are small strings for keys (64–128b) and the KV index churns. flame shows spikes in `makeKeyFromParts` after sanitizer change.

Jamal: hypothesis: per-request salt introduced accidentally; change increased key diversity, reduced cross-request reuse, caused eviction churn, and eventually growth because old KV entries stick around until compaction and eviction windows finish.

Maria: quick mitigation options? 1) revert sanitizer change for streaming path; 2) switch sanitizer to `session_salt || tenant_salt` (prefer session) so sticky sessions still coalesce; 3) increase compaction frequency temporarily.

Alex: my +1 for option 2 as quick patch — preserve dedupe for existing clients that rely on prefix sticky reuse. reverting is disruptive to landing other fixes.

Sophie: we should also add a test that simulates longctx traffic with repeated prefixes and check reuse_rate >= 60% in CI.

Jamal: agree. I'll open a PR to change sanitizer behavior and add a smoke test. will also attach the `kv_reuse` metric to the canary dashboard (current alert threshold already breached).

infra-bot: perf-alert: `kv_reuse_rate` (canary) dropped below 0.25 for >5m — ticket created: INF-2026-1423.

Maria: TY. Jamal can you add the offending stack traces and the small repro script to the ticket?

Jamal: doing it now. will post updates in this thread and assign the canary rollback flag if patch looks risky.

Alex: if we decide to fallback to session affinity for keys we should document the semantics in prefix-keying.md (so future sanitizer changes don't regress).

Sophie: also run the longctx run with current batching settings and one with `batch_max_tokens` halved — to see if batching changes amplify eviction churn.

Jamal: noted. timeline: patch + smoke test within 2h, canary metric watch for 1h after deploy.

Maria: :thumbsup: thanks everyone.
